section_1_unit_metadata.essay_title: Rhetorical Protopolitics in Heidegger and Arendt
section_1_unit_metadata.author: Theodore Kisiel
section_1_unit_metadata.essay_thesis: Heidegger's 1923-24 confrontation with Aristotle's Rhetoric and Politics produces a 'rhetorical protopolitics' equiprimordial with the Aristotelian threefold definition of the human being (logon echon, zoon politikon, praxical being-in-the-world); this protopolitics frames Heidegger's first concept of polis as phenomenological speech-community (1923-25) but mutates into a metontological will-of-the-people polis (1933-35) and an archaic-poietic polis of polemos and Heimat (1935-43); Hannah Arendt's Human Condition retrieves the protopolitical strand by radicalizing the Mitwelt as the public space of doxa, opinion, and equiprimordial freedom-of-speech-and-action.
section_1_unit_metadata.structure_note: ESSAY HAS 9 ROMAN SECTIONS, NOT 7 AS RECORDED IN PHASE 0/PHASE 1. The Phase 0 audit recorded I-VII; the actual essay has VIII (THE ARCHAIC PREPOLITICAL POLIS, p. 151) and IX (ARENDT'S PUBLIC SPACE OF DOXA, p. 153). Section VII (THE METONTOLOGICAL POLIS OF NATIONAL SOCIALISM) ends at p. 151; the Antigone/Hölderlin material Phase 0 placed under VII actually constitutes Section VIII; the entire Arendt material constitutes Section IX. The inline 3-phase polis table (p. 149) sits at the close of Section VI, framing the move from VII (Metontological) into VIII (Archaic-Poietic). Phase 2 records the 9-section structure as the authoritative reading.

section_2_outline.heading: [Opening — no heading]
bullets: Frames 1923 as 'annus terribilis' for postwar Germany: Versailles Treaty's punitive effects, Weimar parliamentary fiscal-policy crisis, French occupation of the Ruhr, the general strike, Hitler's Munich putsch, Mein Kampf dictation in prison.

Heidegger's Dasein-ontology develops in 1923 against this backdrop via 'wholesale confrontation' with Aristotle's Rhetoric and Politics — the three Aristotelian definitions of the human (logon echon, zoon politikon, practical being-in-the-world) read as 'equally primordial.'

Modern German Dasein figured as 'newspaper-reader': the rhetorical locus shifts from the orality of the Greek polis to the 'predominant textuality' of postwar pulp media. Context-dependent temporality of crisis-speech is what attracts Heidegger.

Two 'occasional pieces' become the sites of confrontation: the December 1924 Köln Ruhr-tour talk 'Dasein und Wahrsein nach Aristoteles' (Interpretation von Buch 6 der Nikomachischen Ethik), and SS 1924 'Grundbegriffe der aristotelischen Philosophie' (Löwith transcript: 'Aristoteles: Rhetorik II').

Aristotle's Rhetoric — not Plato's Republic — is the more ontological Greek Urtext of political philosophy at this 'early stage' of Heidegger's political development. The rhetorical politics of crisis-speech is the matter situated ontologically.

The everydayness of being-with-one-another is interpreted (SZ 85: 'already having been interpreted') by a particular tradition of usage of the discursive space; this is the perfect-aprioric basis from which the rhetorical politics of a time takes its cues.

section_2_outline.heading: I. 1923-24: 'BEING-HERE AND BEING-TRUE ACCORDING TO ARISTOTLE'
bullets: Locates the 'Ruhr-Rede' (1923-24 lecture-tour talk on Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics VI): drafted late 1923 at peak Ruhr crisis, delivered final form Dec 1924 in Cologne with Max Scheler as host; structurally anticipates 'On the Essence of Truth' (1930-43).

Argues the talk's distinctive contribution: dispatch of the apophantic/declarative judgment as primary locus of truth in favor of the more practical and crucial krinein in everyday speech situations — the public space of polis as 'clearing of be-ing.'

Lists the Aristotelian three civic genres (deliberative, judicial, epideictic) with explicit application to 1923-24 Germany: deliberative = the November-betrayal propaganda, judicial = Hitler's putsch trial, epideictic = the Schlageter commemoration.

Documents Heidegger's own epideictic protopolitics: his May 26, 1933 Schlageter speech as Rector — given the day before his more famous Rectoral Address — celebrating Schlageter's 'hardest death' as native son of the Black Forest, his 'true,' 'constant,' 'faithful,' 'loyal' (treu) virtue (SZ 385, 391).

Heidegger's 1924 summary of the elements of Aristotelian civic rhetoric for protopractical ontology of everydayness: (1) deliberation/judgment/relishing as temporality of polis-speech-genres; (2) the three pisteis (pathos most basic, ethos, deiknynai/logos); (3) ethos as not just personal but throwness of speaker into speech; (4) deiknynai as enthymeme (en-thymos, 'to the heart') drawing on doxa, gnomic maxims, sound-bite cliché.

Heidegger's three modes of concealment/three modes of 'trueing' — two attributed directly to language of rhetoric: (1) bringing beings to fore via initial/immediate opinions; (2) pressing into unfamiliar original domains; (3) Kampf against the concealing catchphrase and cliché (Titanenkampf, gigantomachia).

Bridges to Aristotle's NE VI: five excellent habits of being-true (techne or poiesis, phronesis or praxis, episteme, sophia, nous); two pretheoretical practical ones (techne, phronesis) become the 'two ways of coping' = the two divisions of BT; phronesis = action of resoluteness receptive to call of conscience.

section_2_outline.heading: II. SS 1924: GROUND CONCEPTS OF ARISTOTELIAN PHILOSOPHY
bullets: Frames the SS 1924 course (GA 18) project: understand Aristotle's ground concepts in their 'native growth' from native soil (Bodenständigkeit) of the Greek language — i.e., from the doxa of ordinary everyday speech.

Of Metaphysics V's 30 lexical entries for 'being,' ousia is the most important — discovered by Heidegger to mean 'constant presence' for the Greek titans (Aristotle included) since Parmenides; but its native-soil practical roots are domestic property (Habe/having; German Anwesen = real estate also = 'presence').

Heidegger's 'lifelong project' announced here: replacing 'being-as-having' / habit operative in the Greek fixation on eternal real estate with the kairological language of a German Da-sein 'always dispossessed, thrown into the world temporally.'
Practical and political life of the 'living being possessive of speech' = the life that 'repeatedly encounters changeable being.'
Crucial passage in Kisiel: emphasis on hearing (akouein) over seeing as fundamental mode of perception (GA 18, 44); aneu logou — nous as without speech, beyond language.

section_2_outline.heading: III. THE PUBLIC GENERIC ANYONE
bullets: Speech makes the world manifest; communicative sharing manifests being-with-one-another in 'mutual accord and active concert' = the locus of the political. 'I am one-among-many' as ontological how-of-being, not ontic fact.

Anyone (das Man) = 'true bearer of the peculiar universal of averageness' is our language (GA 18 64); domineering prevalence of Anyone in language = doxa, the usually tacit major premises of rhetoric (73).

Distinguishes 'hoi aristoi' (the few who excel) from 'das Man, hoi polloi' (the many) as 'public kind of power of apathy and indifference built into the repeatability of language' = baseline category of properly political ontology.
Rhetorical-political realm of language circumscribing self-evidence of public opinion (73) = basis for the universal validity of agreement in objective sciences (64).
But Heidegger formally outlines path OUT of levelling impersonal anonymity via 'communication and struggle (Kampf)' (SZ 384) — actualizing historical uniqueness and self-identity of community.

Critical claim against Bourdieu/Marcuse/Arendt readers: the Anyone is not historical (SZ 300), but 'authentic with-one-another' arises 'from the authentic self-being of resolute openness' (SZ 298); 'fateful destiny of Dasein in and with its generation' (SZ 384f) constitutes the 'full authentic historical happening of Dasein.'

section_2_outline.heading: IV. THE POLITICAL LIFE AS HISTORICAL
bullets: Discriminates Aristotle's three life-styles (NE I): bios apolaustikos (pleasure), bios politikos (political), bios theoretikos (theoretical) — each with telos and reward.
Bios politikos has communal goals (vs. individual): economic distribution, social peace within commonweal; teleic closure of communal self-sufficiency.
Public discussion's task: discriminate useful/inexpedient, fitting/improper, just/unjust = competence of prudent statesman/public speaker.
Goal of bios politikos = time, honor, endoxon, recognition amplified by doxa of public esteem (Schlageter's death, Heidegger's commitment to Nazi cause as exemplary endoxon).
The bios politikos depends on 'opinion of the many' — temporal and temporary — addressed in particular situations (kairos), in the crisis of krinein (discriminating judgment).
Of the three life-styles, ONLY bios politikos manifests the full temporality of being 'which can also be otherwise' = motivates Heidegger's protopractical ontology of historical being.

Pathos = intrinsically upsetting, peace-disturbing, even revolutionary — emotions move and make for history. Bios politikos takes a measured Greek look at the 'full tumult of life in motion' postwar Germany witnessed.

section_2_outline.heading: V. EQUIPRIMORDIAL MODES OF PERSUASION AND TRUST (TRUTH)
bullets: Aristotle's Rhetoric for Heidegger = 'hermeneutics of everydayness in crisis' — radically disturbed everydayness exposed for ontological examination. Greek Da-sein in metabole (abrupt transition) being translated into analytic of Da-sein.

The three modes of persuasion (pathos, ethos, logos) become close kin to three modes of 'being-in' / disclosedness: dispositivity (Befindlichkeit), understanding (Verstehen), discursivity (Rede). Equiprimordiality is THE key claim.

Hearing (auditor) as also for the rhetor = component first having to size up critical speech situation — phronimos who responds with prudent counsel = phronesis = capacity to listen to (heed, hear) call of (communal) conscience. Hearing is being possessed by speech.
Listening at level of orexis (desire/care/concern) = most rudimentary type of understanding — found in life of pathos, mood. Speech finds deepest roots in mood (GA 18 177).

GA 18 165: 'ethos and pathos are constitutive for legein itself.' Equiprimordiality, convertibility, interchangeability of basic terms of conviction/trust/confidence: ethos, logos (first as doxa, enthymema), pathos.

Interchangeability of speaker/auditor roles: speaker first auditor to oneself (one's 'conscience') while auditor 'speaks simply by auditing.' BT: 'attuned silence may well be the most authentic form of speaking.'
Aristotle's not-yet-logos appeal to passions and call to future action — the unspoken alogon of orexis 'is itself a kind of speech' (GA 18 105).

To ethos = general bearing/figure one cuts; behaving, manner of holding-oneself in/toward world (GA 18 68, 165). In deliberative speech, ethos translates into prohairesis (prechoice) — fundamental option in polity/policy that constitutes purpose of speech.

Heidegger's framework: ethos translates into Entschlossenheit manifested in speaker's conviction-display; speaker's resoluteness brings others to same resolution = kairos = moment of decision in polity/policy (171).

Resoluteness = receptive response to call of conscience. Politician projects self as authentic conscience for other (SZ 122, 298) via 'leaping ahead and liberating' — but inauthentically 'leaps in and dominates the other' = Fürsorge of welfare state.

Rhetoric itself = first not art but power, dynamis (GA 18 114). Not power of persuasion (sophist's reading) but cultivated power of situational insight, phronesis, 'be-ing able to see, hear, and feel,' temporally particular situation 'je nach dem.'

Later Heidegger's 'middle-voiced turn' from logos/pathos/ethos: from human being to situation of being itself. Heraclitean ethos as (1) haunt/abode/accustomed place, (2) Brauch (custom/usage/habit-of-habitat), (3) history and destiny of a people in shared actional topoi.

Authentic doxa: distinction between civil rhetoric of Greeks vs. propaganda rhetoric of postwar Weimar = present in 1924 but muted in BT — between authentic and inauthentic doxa. (1) matter-of-course concealment in folk-wisdom-everyday-rhetoric; (2) malicious concealment of obfuscating catchphrase/cliché.

Doxa as 'authentic discoveredness of being-with-one-another in the world' (149) — average intelligibility in which Anyone moves; doxa-incorporates negotiating-with-one-another (Verhandeln: parley, deliberate, plead, discuss, debate); ground/source/result of speaking-with-one-another (151).

Practically, doxa is conditioned by politics (134); seeks resolute action (entschlossenes Handeln, 145). Tests: speaker like good statesman risen above partial views to oversight of whole problematic situation, kairos, full temporal horizon? Speaker resolute and prudent? Speaker attuned to mood (162)?

section_2_outline.heading: VI. THE FATE OF RHETORIC IN THE LATER HEIDEGGER
bullets: Brief transitional section: 'The later Heidegger will develop two additional concepts of the political.'
Followed immediately by the inline TABLE 'Heidegger's Three Concepts of Polis and the Political' (p. 149).

Table presented as authoritative tripartite scheme; calls for 'only a quick tracing of the fate of rhetoric across these remaining concepts of the polis and the political.' Note 9 cross-references Kisiel's 'In the Middle of Heidegger's Three Concepts of the Political' (Raffoul/Pettigrew 2002).

section_2_outline.heading: VII. THE METONTOLOGICAL POLIS OF NATIONAL SOCIALISM
bullets: Two basic existentials: a people and its state, connected by crucial political act of historical decision (phronesis) by which a people 'decide for the state appropriate to its unique tradition (ethos) and freely unite to support and maintain it.'
National socialism modeled on WWI 'front community' (Frontgemeinschaft); University Rector Heidegger's role in 'worker state of three services (labor, defense, knowledge), based on Führer principle.'
Political education of 'guardians' (Hüter) — future state leaders cultivated within University.

Quotes the Rectoral seminar of WS 1933-34 ('Vom Wesen und Begriff von Natur, Geschichte und Staat'): 'Each man and woman must learn that their individual lives decides the destiny of the people and the state, supports or rejects it.'
Centrality of will: willpower founds/sustains/rules state — through acknowledgment will of leader (Führer), state enforces by ruling.

Heidegger's use of central German-idealist 'will' is conditioned by understanding it 'wholly in terms of Aristotle's political virtue, phronesis': will as engaging pursuit of goal dictated by situation; 'will deliberatively grasps the situation in the fullness of its time, in it the kairos is at work.'

Persuasion by speech or by deed — Greek instinct made persuasive power of speech a paradigm of politics (Thucydides). Führer's 'drumming' style of 'propagandizing' (Trommelnder) = unconscious acknowledgement of power of speech rhetoric had uncovered politically (in pisteis of rhetorical politics: see Section V).
True rule manifests true knowledge of goal — wisdom of statesman (phronimos) — engagement, perseverance, staying-power.

True effectuation: not coercion but 'awakening the same willing in the other' = re-creation of others to accord with mood/temper of ruling will. Decision on part of individual, not momentary yes-saying.

Will of leader 're-creates the others in a following out of which a community arises' = vital solidarity of followers to leader. Other forms of putting state will into effect (governance, justice) follow from will of people on its way to becoming Führerstaat (leader state).

Highest actualization of human being = in the state. Quotes Luther: 'Si gesturus principatus ut sciam rem esse populi non meam privatam' [To assume the mantle of leadership is to understand affairs of people are not my private affair].

section_2_outline.heading: VIII. THE ARCHAIC PREPOLITICAL POLIS
bullets: Heidegger's growing disenchantment with 'Führer turning from statesmanlike to coercive ways' = post-1935 reduction of polis to a 'prepolitical originarity' that is source of political, philosophical, poetic, religious creative endeavors.

Read through Sophocles' Antigone tragic phronesis (conflict between family piety and royal ediction): polis is not Staat (geographical state) or Stadt (city) but a 'historical site (Stätte)' = ontological site of Da-sein where unique humankind 'takes place' (statt-findet, statt-hat) = 'granted stead' (gestattet, 'permitted') = 'leeway' (Spielraum) of allotted time/historical place = unique 'homestead' (Heimstatt).

Historical site of Da-sein = 'pole' of polis from which human beings receive stance/status. 'Politics' in supreme/authentic sense takes place at supreme site of radical historical transition displayed by Greek tragedy.

Antigone glossed as hypsipolis apolis (lofty-city/no-city) — 'far beyond and without home and site, unhomely, lonesome, uncanny' — 'singled out for lofty greatness by creating a new home for her people, as well as for the precipitous destruction.'
Heidegger's contemporary heroes likewise: Hölderlin, Nietzsche, van Gogh, Schlageter — all shared this fate of 'lofty greatness' destined to destruction.
Around this 'core of history,' Da-sein as polis: not just statesmen/thinkers but poets/prophets gathered together in 'unity and lonely, untimely, tragic, and contentious dialogue.'

Hölderlin's 'land of poets and thinkers,' 'fatherland' — politics finds origins in poetizing and thinking: 'It is from these two prior activities that the Dasein of a people is made fully effective as a people through to the state — politics' (GA 39 214).

Heidegger's archaic critique of Nazi totalitarianism (GA 39 51): 'These [Nazi] enthusiasts are now suddenly discovering the political everywhere... But the polis cannot be defined politically.... Perhaps the name polis is precisely the word for that realm that constantly became questionable anew.'

Aristotle on man as political-because-zoon-logon-echon — but he 'did not see the full uncanniness that membership in the polis brings, far outstripping the rhetorical as well as the political of a people's state.'
Hölderlin's 'Since we are a conversation / and can hear from one another' — refers to 'thoughtful dialogue among solitary creators (poets, thinkers, statesmen) at the very abysses of being.'
Language = original institution of being in the violent words of poetic origin, NOT means of communication for sake of quick agreement (= rhetoric).

Community of creators = combative community of struggle over extreme issues of being. Coming-to-an-understanding = combat: 'Conversation here is not communication, but the fundamental happening of radical exposure in the thick of beings' (GA 53 102) — polemos.

section_2_outline.heading: IX. ARENDT'S PUBLIC SPACE OF DOXA
bullets: Hannah Arendt's first encounter with Heidegger: WS 1924-25 lecture course on Plato's Sophist (which began with summary of his SS 1924 work on Aristotle). Unclear whether Arendt accessed any 1924 student transcripts.
Her work nonetheless 'protopolitics of human condition' marked by 'uniquely phenomenological approach to the Greek polis.'

Aristotle's Rhetoric sometimes drawn on for protopolitical points: distinction between solitary in (philosophy/thinking) and political plural between (public communication generates political arena of action).

Genus-species structure of Aristotle's definitions of man (singular 'man' as if single human nature) misses 'temporal particularity' (Jeweiligkeit) — early Heidegger interprets these definitions despite the slip.

Arendt's interpretation: man as zoon politikon and logon echon = 'insofar as he is political he has the faculty of speech, the power to understand, to make himself understood, and to persuade' (Arendt, Essays in Understanding 442).

Highest, 'truly political art' = rhetoric — cultivated by free men in Greek polis. Arendt's phenomenology more protopolitical than Aristotle's: reaches back to 'grass-roots politics' of associations preceding institutionalized assemblies/judicial systems.

Human Condition = critical appropriation of Heidegger's Daseins-analytic learned at Marburg. Three levels of human activities: labor (private/household), work (environing/things), action (interhuman world = Mitwelt).
Climaxes in radicalization of Heidegger's Mitwelt as concept of the political. 'Plurality and natality' = facticity of entire world of human affairs.
Politics (Arendt): 'based on fact of plurality of human beings... organize and regulate the being-together of different and not equal beings' (Human Condition 175).
Equality of mutuality: humans share equally in capacity for mutual communication; plurality signifies personal uniqueness, equality enables community.

It is not in man as political animal but BETWEEN humans as its very space, that politics arises: freedom and spontaneity = 'very content and sense of politics is freedom' (Arendt, Between Past and Future 154f).
Two forms of freedom-of-movement in this public space: (1) freedom to begin something new and unprecedented (natality of being-there); (2) freedom to move among many and speak with them.

Polis = 'public space of freedom — realm where freedom is a worldly reality, tangible in words... in deeds... in events... incorporated into the great storybook of human history' (Arendt, Between Past and Future 263).

Arendt calls this public space the 'space of appearance,' of dokein/doxa in twofold Greek sense: 'opinion' AND 'splendor, fame, repute' (Ansicht and Ansehen in German) — how things look to me and how I look to others.
Doubles back to Aristotelian rhetorical speech-situation: doxic content of speech itself + ethos of speaker before judgment of audience.

'Space of appearance' = where 'I go public,' 'make an appearance,' 'make my debut' — Greeks established polis to multiply opportunities to 'distinguish oneself, show in deed and word who one was in his unique distinctness' = 'immortal fame' or ignoble shame.

But agonal spirit can degenerate: doxa multiplies world into 'pluralized space of appearances' that threatens anarchy: 'battlefield of partial, conflicting interests' = 'national vice of ancient Greece.'

Aristotle's antidote: friendship (philia) as 'real bond of community' more basic than justice (Plato's Republic). Friends = equal partners in common world dispensing with hierarchy. Doxa as 'true opinion' — insight, partial, into reality of common world.

Kant's 'enlarged mentality' / cosmopolitan 'common sense' = guide to prudential judgments of the phronetic statesman; sensus communis as 'a sense common to all... faculty of judgment which... takes account of mode of representation of all other men.'

Common sense = ability to look beyond one's POV and see things from perspective of all involved. Statesman's outstanding virtue: understand 'greatest number of divergent realities... open themselves up to opinions of citizens' = communicate between citizens to bring out reality of common world.
Cosmopolitan ethos of Kant converges with ethos of political speaker detailed by Aristotle: phronesis kai arete kai eunoia = 'good sense, goodness, and good will' (Aristotle, Rhetoric 2.1, 1378a10).
These character-traits of common sense applied to contemporary statesman in adjudicating expert opinion vs. common good: 'Hiroshima, the Cuban missile crisis, and 9/11-01.'

Final critique of Heidegger: Arendt 'never addressed Heidegger's brief but fateful commitment to NS' but knew enough from published record to pinpoint 'where Heidegger's thought had been infected with bacillus of totalitarianism.'

Heidegger's early solipsistic existentialism (authentic Self distancing from public Anyone, becoming 'representative of no one but itself') — countered by 'mythologizing confusions like Folk and Earth' to supply isolated Selves with shared common ground.

Concluding diagnosis: nature-oriented superstition (primal myth of autochthony / Bodenständigkeit) of landed gentry, peasant folk rooted in earth = 'mechanical reconciliation of atomized selves in a common ground alien to their nature... selves intent on willing themselves into an Overself in order somehow to make the transition from guilt, accepted in resoluteness, to action.'

section_2_outline.table_significance: The volume's most articulated single position-statement on Heidegger's political trajectory. Captures the displacement of Aristotle's Rhetoric (the rhetorical-protopolitical first phase) by Plato's Republic (the metontological-Führer-state phase) by Sophocles' Antigone (the archaic-poietic-polemos phase). Only Phase 1 is rhetorical; rhetoric is progressively abandoned in Phases 2-3. Cross-referenced to Kisiel's 'In the Middle of Heidegger's Three Concepts of the Political' (Raffoul/Pettigrew 2002) per note 9.

section_3_concepts.name: rhetorical protopolitics
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: The rudimentary politics taking shape in Heidegger's emerging fundamental ontology of 1923-24, in which the everydayness of being-with-one-another (a speech-community whose telos is Verstandigung/communication-and-accord) sediments a 'politics' equiprimordial with rhetoric — speech-as-political. Not full political philosophy but the protopractical layer that frames the speech-situation as already political.

section_3_concepts.name: annus terribilis 1923
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Kisiel's framing of 1923 as the historical-rhetorical scene against which Heidegger develops his protopractical ontology: Versailles punitive effects, Weimar fiscal crisis, French Ruhr occupation, general strike, Munich putsch, Mein Kampf. The rhetorical politics of crisis-speech is the matter Heidegger situates ontologically.

section_3_concepts.name: modern Dasein as newspaper-reader
section_3_concepts.english_form: the living being who reads the newspapers
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Heidegger's 1924 figure for modern German Dasein: zoon logon echon now in the textual register of pulp media reporting from far and wide, replacing the Greek polis's predominant orality. Public discursive space mediated through textuality 'just as transient as oral speech,' governed by vicissitudes of place and time — i.e., 'context-dependent temporality.'

section_3_concepts.name: rhetoric as dynamis (not techne)
section_3_concepts.english_form: rhetoric as power, capacity (not as art/technique)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Following Aristotle Rhetoric I.2 (and Gadamer's testimony in Ch 2), rhetoric for Heidegger is 'first of all not an art but a power, dynamis' — not the sophist's power of persuasion but cultivated power of situational insight, phronesis, 'be-ing able to see, hear, and feel,' temporally particular situation 'je nach dem' (GA 18 114).

section_3_concepts.name: the public generic Anyone (das Man)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: True bearer of the universal of averageness = our language (GA 18 64). Domineering prevalence of Anyone in language = doxa, the tacit major premises of rhetoric (73). Distinct from hoi aristoi (the few who excel) and from hoi polloi as 'public kind of power of apathy and indifference built into the repeatability of language' = baseline category of properly political ontology.

section_3_concepts.name: Öffentlichkeit (publicness)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: The sphere of Anyone-self-evidence, the rhetorical-political realm of language that circumscribes self-evidence of public opinion (GA 18 73), basis for universal validity of agreement in objective sciences (64). Critically distinguished from authentic-with-one-another arising from resolute openness (SZ 298).

section_3_concepts.name: communication and struggle (Mitteilung und Kampf)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: SZ 384 formula: the path 'out of levelling impersonal anonymity' to 'authentic grouping by actualizing the historical uniqueness and self-identity of community.' Kisiel emphasizes the two as 'rhetorical dimensions' that motivate the leveling-Anyone's inverse — the historical destiny of Dasein in and with its 'generation' = 'full authentic historical happening of Dasein' (SZ 384f).

section_3_concepts.name: equiprimordial modes of persuasion and trust
section_3_concepts.english_form: equiprimordial three pisteis = three modes of being-in (Befindlichkeit/Verstehen/Rede)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Aristotle's three pisteis (pathos, ethos, logos) become close kin to three modes of disclosedness of human situation (dispositivity, understanding, discursivity). Equiprimordiality, convertibility, interchangeability of conviction-trust-confidence terms: ethos, logos (first as doxa, enthymema), pathos. GA 18 165: 'ethos and pathos are constitutive for legein itself.'

section_3_concepts.name: pistis equiprimordial with aletheia
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Section V's titular thesis: persuasion (the three pisteis) and trust are equiprimordial with truth (modes of trueing/unconcealment). Speech finds deepest roots in mood (pathos, GA 18 177); the not-yet-logos appeal to passions and call to future action — alogon of orexis 'is itself a kind of speech' (105).

section_3_concepts.name: authentic doxa
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Doxa as 'authentic discoveredness of being-with-one-another in the world' (GA 18 149). Average intelligibility in which Anyone moves; doxa incorporates 'negotiating-with-one-another' (Verhandeln); ground/source/result of speaking-with-one-another (151). Distinguished from inauthentic doxa = malicious concealment of obfuscating catchphrase/cliché.

section_3_concepts.name: ethos translated into Entschlossenheit
section_3_concepts.english_form: resoluteness as translation of Aristotelian ethos
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Heidegger's framework: ethos (general bearing, manner-of-holding-oneself in/toward world) translates into Entschlossenheit manifested in speaker's display of conviction (GA 18 171). Resoluteness = receptive response to call of conscience. Speaker's resoluteness brings others to same resolution = kairos = moment of decision in polity/policy.

section_3_concepts.name: phronesis as rhetorical-political virtue
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Phronimos = statesman whose responsiveness to crisis-situation generates prudent counsel; capacity to listen to (heed, hear) call of (communal) conscience. Phronesis = action of resoluteness receptive to call of conscience (NE VI). In SS 1933-34 Heidegger's 'will' is conditioned wholly in terms of Aristotle's phronesis: 'will deliberatively grasps the situation in the fullness of its time, in it the kairos is at work.'

section_3_concepts.name: leaping ahead vs. leaping in (Fürsorge)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Politician projects self as authentic conscience for other through prescient insight 'leaping ahead and liberating' (SZ 122, 298). Inauthentically, politician 'leaps in and dominates the other' = makes other dependent on welfare state. Rhetorical reading of solicitude: 'politics and pedagogy' combined.

section_3_concepts.name: the metontological polis
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Heidegger's second polis-concept (1933-35, Plato Republic-based): two basic existentials (a people and its state) connected by crucial political act of historical decision (phronesis); state as 'leader of people, guardians of state, 3-level service' (labor/defense/knowledge); Führer principle; political education of guardians (Hüter).

section_3_concepts.name: Führerstaat / leader-state
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Heidegger's WS 1933-34 conception: highest actualization of human being in the state; state-of-three-services with guardians as future leaders cultivated within University; will of leader 'awakens the same willing in the other' = re-creation of others to accord with mood of ruling will. Persuasion by speech (Trommelnder) and by deed.

section_3_concepts.name: the archaic-poietic polis (polemos)
section_3_concepts.english_form: the archaic prepolitical site of being
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Heidegger's third polis-concept (1935-43, Sophocles Antigone-based): polis is not Staat or Stadt but 'historical site (Stätte)' where unique humankind 'takes place' = 'pole' from which beings receive stance. Polemos of thinker, poet, and statesman as prepolitical. Hölderlin's 'land of poets and thinkers' / 'fatherland.' Language = original institution of being in violent words of poetic origin, NOT means of communication for sake of agreement.

section_3_concepts.name: Antigone as hypsipolis apolis
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Sophocles' Antigone as supreme exemplar: tragic heroine 'far beyond and without home and site, unhomely, lonesome, uncanny' — singled out for 'lofty greatness by creating a new home for her people, as well as for the precipitous destruction.' Heidegger's contemporary heroes (Hölderlin, Nietzsche, van Gogh, Schlageter) share this fate.

section_3_concepts.name: polemos as fundamental conversation
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Hölderlin's 'Since we are a conversation / and can hear from one another' = thoughtful dialogue among solitary creators at abysses of being. Coming-to-an-understanding = combat: 'Conversation here is not communication, but the fundamental happening of radical exposure in the thick of beings' (GA 53 102).

section_3_concepts.name: Bodenständigkeit (autochthony)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Two registers: (1) AS GREEK PHILOSOPHICAL METHOD: ground concepts in their 'native growth' from native soil of Greek language (the doxa of ordinary speech, Section II); (2) AS HEIDEGGER'S NAZI-PERIOD MYTHOLOGY: 'primal myth of autochthony of a landed gentry, a peasant folk rooted in the earth from which they first sprang and which thus constitutes their native ground' — diagnosed by Kisiel as nature-oriented superstition and 'mechanical reconciliation of atomized selves in a common ground alien to their nature.'

section_3_concepts.name: Verstandigung (understanding-agreement)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Telos of fundamental speaking-with-one-another: 'a coming to an understanding agreement (Verständigung) with one another, hermeneia, communication and the accord that it brings in the public sphere.' From this fundamental speaking-with-one-another the rudimentary protopolitics begins (GA 18 45f, 122f, 241).

section_3_concepts.name: Jeweiligkeit (temporal particularity)
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Heidegger's 'temporally particularizing universals' (jeweilige Universalia) = peculiarly temporal universals sensitive not only to distributive 'each' (jede) but also to varying temporal contexts 'je nach dem.' Resists Aristotle's genus-species structure in defining man (Section IX, Arendt critique).

section_3_concepts.name: Mitwelt as space of plurality and natality
section_3_concepts.english_form: interhuman world as space of action
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Arendt's radicalization of Heidegger's Mitwelt: third level of human activity (with labor and work) where 'I from birth already find myself thrown together with others.' Politics arises BETWEEN humans (not in man as zoon politikon). Plurality and natality = 'facticity of entire world of human affairs.'

section_3_concepts.name: doxa as space of appearance
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Arendt's twofold Greek sense: 'opinion' AND 'splendor, fame, repute' (German Ansicht and Ansehen) — how things look to me and how I look to others. Doubles back to Aristotelian rhetorical situation: doxic content of speech + ethos of speaker. Polis multiplies opportunities to 'distinguish oneself' = win 'immortal fame' or ignoble shame.

section_3_concepts.name: enlarged mentality / sensus communis
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Arendt invokes Kant's 'enlarged mentality' / cosmopolitan 'common sense' = guide to prudential judgments of phronetic statesman. 'A sense common to all, a faculty of judgment which, in its reflection, takes account of mode of representation of all other men' (Critique of Judgment §40). Converges with Aristotle's phronesis kai arete kai eunoia (Rhetoric 2.1, 1378a10).

section_3_concepts.name: the Schlageter epideictic
section_3_concepts.definition_in_essay: Heidegger's first political speech for new Nazi regime, given day before Rectoral Address. Epideictic celebration of Schlageter's 'hardest death' as native son of Black Forest, 'true,' 'constant,' 'faithful,' 'loyal' (treu) virtue (SZ 385, 391) — foundation upon Heidegger's 'own ontic-existentiell ideal of a pantheon of heroes determined by his German ethos.' Read by Kisiel as exemplification of Aristotelian epideictic genus operating politically.

section_4_positions.claim: Heidegger's 1923-24 confrontation with Aristotle's Rhetoric (and secondarily Politics, NE) produces a 'rhetorical protopolitics' equiprimordial with the threefold definition of the human (logon echon, zoon politikon, practical being-in-the-world); rhetoric is therefore not a side-room of fundamental ontology but constitutive of it at the level of the everyday speech-situation.
premises: Aristotle's three definitions of man are 'equally primordial' (Heidegger reads them so).
The everyday speech-situation IS the political situation of being-with-one-another (Mitsein).
Telos of speaking-with-one-another = Verständigung (hermeneia, communication-and-accord); this is the rudimentary site of polis.
GA 18 §§45f, 122f, 241 — the protopolitical layer of Heidegger's emerging fundamental ontology.
targets: Pöggeler's 'restricted' thesis (HR-07-POGGELER): Kisiel insists the protopolitical reach of GA 18 is broader than Pöggeler concedes.
Bourdieu/Marcuse readings of das Man as primarily sociological-political: Kisiel insists the existentiale Anyone is also the path OUT via SZ 298 'authentic with-one-another.'

section_4_positions.claim: Heidegger's three concepts of polis — Phenomenological (1923-25, Aristotle's Rhetoric), Metontological (1933-35, Plato's Republic), Archaic-Poietic (1935-43, Sophocles' Antigone) — form a strict succession in which only the FIRST is rhetorical; rhetoric is progressively displaced by the will-of-the-Führer (in II) and by the polemos-of-poetic-origin (in III).
premises: GA 18 SS 1924 (rhetorical) → WS 1933-34 'Vom Wesen und Begriff von Natur, Geschichte und Staat' (metontological) → GA 39 (1934-35) and GA 53 (1942) (archaic-poietic) document a textual succession of polis-concepts.
Each phase has a 'basic text' (Aristotle Rhetoric / Plato Republic / Sophocles Antigone) and 'basic concepts' (pathos/ethos/logos / leader-guardians-services / polemos).

The displacement is itself rhetorically traceable: Heidegger's later disenchantment with Führer state turns to Hölderlin's 'land of poets and thinkers,' redefining language as 'original institution of being in violent words of poetic origin' rather than 'means of communication for sake of quick easy agreement (rhetoric)' (GA 53 102).
targets: Continuist readings that flatten 1924-1933-1942 into a single Heideggerian project.

Pöggeler's monolithic 'restricted' reading: Kisiel insists rhetoric IS restricted, but that the ARC of restriction is itself politically diagnostic (reflects move toward Führer-will and then toward poetic-polemos).

section_4_positions.claim: The metontological polis of National Socialism is Heidegger's mistaken phronetic translation of Aristotle's political virtue: Heidegger reads German-idealist 'will' (Führerwille, Volkswille) wholly in terms of Aristotelian phronesis — 'will deliberatively grasps the situation in the fullness of its time, in it the kairos is at work' — but the situation he so 'grasps' is the propaganda-political situation he himself diagnosed in 1924 as the inauthentic doxa of the catchphrase.
premises: Heidegger's 1924 inauthentic-doxa critique distinguishes 'civil rhetoric of Greeks' from 'propaganda rhetoric of postwar Weimar.'
Heidegger's 1933-34 deployment of 'will' is conditioned 'wholly in terms of Aristotle's political virtue, phronesis.'
But the Führer's 'drumming' (Trommelnder) propagandizing-style is the very inauthentic-doxa Heidegger had earlier diagnosed.
Heidegger's 'leaping-in-and-dominating' Fürsorge (welfare-state mode of solicitude, SZ 122) is what the Führerstaat instantiates, not the 'leaping-ahead-and-liberating' authentic mode.
targets: Apologetic readings (mistake-by-temporary-error). Kisiel's reading: the Nazi turn is a phronetic miscalculation traceable to Heidegger's own framework.
Anti-Heideggerian readings that dismiss the rhetorical analysis as merely-Nazi: Kisiel insists the framework is salvageable but the 1933-1935 application is internally diagnostic of failure.

section_4_positions.claim: Heidegger's archaic-poietic turn after 1935 abandons rhetoric proper: language becomes 'original institution of being in the violent words of poetic origin' rather than 'means of communication for sake of quick and easy agreement, rhetoric' (GA 53 102). Polemos replaces rhetoric; conversation = combat, not communication.
premises: GA 39 (Hölderlin's Hymns 'Germanien' and 'Der Rhein,' WS 1934-35), 214, 51 — polis as 'land of poets and thinkers,' politics as origins from poetizing/thinking.
GA 53 (Hölderlin's Hymne 'Der Ister,' SS 1942), 98f, 102 — language as polemos of radical exposure.
Heidegger's own critique of Nazi totalitarianism in GA 39 51: 'These [Nazi] enthusiasts are now suddenly discovering the political everywhere... But the polis cannot be defined politically.'
targets: Readings (Pöggeler implicit) that take the post-1935 'topology of being' as positive replacement.
Continuity-with-rhetoric readings: Kisiel concedes the abandonment, but reframes it as politically diagnostic — the polemos-polis is post-rhetorical, hence post-protopolitical.

section_4_positions.claim: Hannah Arendt's Human Condition recovers the protopolitical strand of GA 18 — without ever directly accessing GA 18 — by radicalizing Heidegger's Mitwelt as the public space of plurality, natality, freedom-of-action and freedom-of-speech. Doxa becomes the 'space of appearance' (dokein in twofold sense of opinion AND splendor/fame), and Aristotle's Rhetoric is restored as the 'highest, truly political art' (Arendt, Essays in Understanding 442).
premises: Arendt's first encounter with Heidegger = WS 1924-25 Plato Sophist course (preceded by summary of his SS 1924).
Human Condition = 'critical appropriation of Heidegger's Daseins-analytic' (Arendt's admission).
Plurality and natality constitute 'the facticity of the entire world of human affairs.'
Politics = 'between humans as its very space' (not 'in man as political animal') = 'the very content and sense of politics is freedom' (Between Past and Future 154f).
Public space = 'space of appearance,' dokein in twofold Greek sense — Aristotle's rhetorical speech-situation (doxic content + ethos of speaker) recurs here.
targets: Anti-Aristotelian readings of Arendt: Kisiel insists Arendt is more protopolitical than Aristotle, reaching back to 'grass-roots politics' before institutionalized assemblies.

section_4_positions.claim: Arendt diagnoses Heidegger's totalitarian moment as bacillus of 'mythologizing confusions like Folk and Earth' supplied 'almost as an afterthought' to compensate for Heidegger's 'early solipsistic existentialism' (authentic Self distancing from public Anyone, becoming 'representative of no one but itself'). The autochthony myth (Bodenständigkeit) is mechanical reconciliation of atomized selves alien to their nature.
premises: Heidegger's Anyone-distancing → solipsistic authentic Self.
Folk and Earth introduced 'almost as afterthought' to supply isolated Selves with shared common ground.
'Primal myth of autochthony of a landed gentry, a peasant folk rooted in the earth' = nature-oriented superstition.
Result: 'organization of selves intent on willing themselves into an Overself in order somehow to make the transition from guilt, accepted in resoluteness, to action.'
targets: Readings that take Heidegger's Folk/Earth motifs as continuous with his early protopolitics.
Bourdieu's 'Heideggerian habitus': Kisiel partly accepts, partly redirects (Marcuse-Olafson 1977 cited as confirming sociological diagnosis from within phenomenological description of das Man).

section_4_positions.claim: Pistis (the three Aristotelian modes of persuasion) is equiprimordial with aletheia (the modes of trueing/unconcealment); rhetoric and truth are not opposed but mutually constitutive at the level of everyday speech-situation. GA 18 165: 'ethos and pathos are constitutive for legein itself.'
premises: Three pisteis (pathos, ethos, logos) close kin to three modes of being-in (Befindlichkeit/Verstehen/Rede).
Speech finds deepest roots in mood/pathos (GA 18 177).
Not-yet-logos appeal to passions = alogon of orexis 'is itself a kind of speech' (105).
Three modes of concealment, three modes of trueing — two attributed by Heidegger directly to language of rhetoric.
targets: Pöggeler's apparent demarcation between rhetoric and truth in 'topology of being.'
Hyde's reading of pathos as merely orator-resource: Kisiel's reading is more ontological, building on Gross's pathos-substrate thesis.

section_5_interlocutors.name: Aristotle
section_5_interlocutors.role: Primary Greek Urtext for protopolitical reading. Three definitions of human (logon echon, zoon politikon, practical being-in-world) read as equiprimordial. Rhetoric as ontological Urtext of political philosophy (more than Plato's Republic 'at this early stage').
citations: Politics I.1-2 (zoon politikon, zoon logon echon)
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: borrowed (the framework); refined (reading the three definitions as equiprimordial rather than genus-species); contrasted (Aristotle 'did not see the full uncanniness that membership in polis brings,' p.152)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Hannah Arendt
section_5_interlocutors.role: Co-titular protagonist. Heidegger's student (1924-26 Marburg); never accessed his GA 18 directly but produced 'protopolitics of human condition' marked by uniquely phenomenological approach to Greek polis; radicalized Heidegger's Mitwelt; restored Aristotle's Rhetoric as 'highest, truly political art'; diagnosed Heidegger's totalitarian bacillus retrospectively. Closes essay as Heidegger's redemptive Arendtian afterlife.
citations: 'What is Existenz Philosophy?' Partisan Review 13 (1946): 34-56, esp. 51
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: borrowed (Heidegger's Mitwelt); refined (radicalized as plurality-natality space); critiqued (silent on Heidegger's Nazi commitment); used to redeem Heidegger's protopolitical strand

section_5_interlocutors.name: Plato
section_5_interlocutors.role: Foil at two levels: (1) Plato's Republic = the OTHER Greek Urtext of political philosophy, displaced for Heidegger by Aristotle's Rhetoric 'at this early stage' (133); (2) but Plato's Republic returns as the 'basic text' of Heidegger's metontological-Nazi-period polis (1933-35) via the leader-guardians-three-services model.
citations: Sophist (WS 1924-25 lecture course = GA 19, Arendt's first Heidegger seminar)
Republic (metontological polis-text 1933-35; antidote-via-friendship at Section IX)
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: contrasted (with Aristotle Rhetoric in Phase 1); appropriated (in Phase 2 metontological); critiqued (the Republic-leadership model = source of Heidegger's Führer-confusion)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Sophocles
section_5_interlocutors.role: Basic text of Heidegger's third (archaic-poietic) polis-concept (1935-43). Antigone glossed as hypsipolis apolis = 'lofty city / no city,' the deina/uncanny tragic heroine = paradigm for Heidegger's contemporary heroes (Hölderlin, Nietzsche, van Gogh, Schlageter).
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: appropriated (by Heidegger as paradigm for archaic-poietic polis); critiqued (by Kisiel through Arendt's later diagnosis of mythologizing turn)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Hölderlin
section_5_interlocutors.role: Poet of 'land of poets and thinkers,' 'fatherland.' Lecture courses GA 39 (Germanien und Rhein, WS 1934-35) and GA 53 (Der Ister, SS 1942) instantiate the Archaic-Poietic polis-phase. Hölderlin's 'Since we are a conversation / and can hear from one another' is reread as polemos = combative-conversation among solitary creators.
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: appropriated (by Heidegger as polemos-poet); critiqued (by Kisiel as occasion of post-rhetorical abandonment)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Schlageter (Albert Leo)
section_5_interlocutors.role: Native son of Black Forest, executed by French firing squad May 1923 (10th anniversary May 1933 = occasion of Heidegger's first political speech as Rector). Read by Kisiel as exemplification of Aristotelian epideictic genus operating politically. Heidegger's Schlageter-speech celebrates 'true,' 'constant,' 'faithful,' 'loyal' (treu) virtue (SZ 385, 391).
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: appropriated (by Heidegger as embodied epideictic ethos); critiqued (by Kisiel as case-study in epideictic-protopolitical-misuse)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Hitler (Adolf)
section_5_interlocutors.role: Foil-rhetorician of postwar German rhetorical situation: Munich putsch trial (1923) = case-study of judicial rhetoric; Mein Kampf dictation = case of rhetorically-charged inauthentic doxa; Führer-Trommelnder = 'unconscious acknowledgement of power of speech that the Greeks had already uncovered politically (in the pisteis of rhetorical politics).' Read AS the inauthentic-doxa-rhetorician Heidegger's framework had earlier diagnosed.
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: contrasted (with Aristotelian civil rhetoric); critiqued (as inauthentic doxa); diagnosed (as unconscious Greek-rhetorical inheritance)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Kant (Immanuel)
section_5_interlocutors.role: Source of 'enlarged mentality' / cosmopolitan 'common sense' (Critique of Judgment §40) that Arendt invokes for prudential judgments of phronetic statesman. Kantian sensus communis = 'sense common to all... faculty of judgment which... takes account of mode of representation of all other men.' Converges with Aristotle's phronesis kai arete kai eunoia.
citations: Critique of Judgment §40 (cited via Arendt, Between Past and Future 220, 241)
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: borrowed (via Arendt) as bridge between modern moral philosophy and Aristotelian rhetorical ethos

section_5_interlocutors.name: Bourdieu (Pierre)
section_5_interlocutors.role: Sociological critic of Heidegger's 'political ontology' read alongside Marcuse-Olafson interview. Both Bourdieu and Marcuse read das Man-description in BT as 'implicit cultural sociology of Weimar and a premonition of disasters of totalitarianism.'
citations: The Political Ontology of Martin Heidegger, trans. Collier (Stanford 1991), 79
Marcuse-Olafson interview, Graduate Faculty Philosophy Journal 6 (1977): 28-40
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: partly accepted (sociological diagnosis from within phenomenological description); partly contrasted (Kisiel insists Heidegger's das Man also formally outlines path OUT via SZ 298)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Marcuse (Herbert)
section_5_interlocutors.role: Heidegger's student (Marburg 1928-32) → critical theorist. Marcuse-Olafson (1977) confirms sociological diagnosis of das Man as Weimar premonition.
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: borrowed (sociological diagnosis); contrasted (Kisiel reads das Man as also opening to authentic-Mitsein via resolute openness)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Mary McCarthy
section_5_interlocutors.role: Arendt's New Yorker friend; her review of Human Condition supplies 'modernized example of theater of appearance': 'Through politics, men reveal not their skill or products [of work] but themselves in their words and actions, held up to admiration or contempt in the free open space of the agora or forum.'
citations: McCarthy, 'The Vita Activa,' On the Contrary (1961), 155-164, esp. 161
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: borrowed (modernizing example of polis-as-public-space, gestures to Union Square / Hyde Park as enduring 'open-air forums')

section_5_interlocutors.name: Max Scheler
section_5_interlocutors.role: Host of Heidegger's December 1924 Cologne Ruhr-tour talk on 'Dasein und Wahrsein nach Aristoteles.' Phenomenological neighborhood; biographical anchor.
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: biographical interlocutor; not engaged conceptually

section_5_interlocutors.name: Karl Löwith
section_5_interlocutors.role: Source of 'Aristoteles: Rhetorik II' transcript-title for SS 1924 course; student transcripts as documentary basis for Heidegger's lectures.
citations: Löwith transcript of SS 1924 ('Aristoteles: Rhetorik II')
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: philological-archival; provides transcript-evidence for argumentative reconstruction

section_5_interlocutors.name: Walter Bröcker
section_5_interlocutors.role: Source of student transcripts for Marburg lectures (named in Phase 0 metadata; implicit in SS 1924 / WS 1924-25 reception).
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: philological-archival

section_5_interlocutors.name: Mark Michalski
section_5_interlocutors.role: Editor of GA 18 (Klostermann 2002). Cross-essay interlocutor (HR-03-MICHALSKI). Supplies the textual edition Kisiel cites as Note 1's 'Henceforth all page references not otherwise specified are to this text.'
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: philological-foundational; Kisiel's Note 1 establishes text-critical authority

section_5_interlocutors.name: Heraclitus
section_5_interlocutors.role: Source of the older sense of ethos to which the later Heidegger turns: ethos as (1) haunt/abode/accustomed place; (2) Brauch (custom/usage/habit-of-habitat); (3) history and destiny of a people in shared actional topoi.
citations: Heraclitean ethos (referenced p.146 via 'older Heraclitean sense')
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: borrowed (by later Heidegger) as alternative to Aristotelian ethos

section_5_interlocutors.name: Luther
section_5_interlocutors.role: Quoted at close of Section VII: 'Si gesturus principatus ut sciam rem esse populi non meam privatam' [To assume the mantle of leadership is to understand that the affairs of the people are not my private affair]. Heidegger invokes 'spirit of Luther' to anchor the Prussian-Lutheran ethos of leadership in royal-elector tradition.
citations: Luther's letter on royal elector (cited via Heidegger WS 1933-34)
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: appropriated (by Heidegger for leader-state legitimation); cited by Kisiel as evidence of Heidegger's deliberate Prussian-Lutheran framing

section_5_interlocutors.name: Husserl
section_5_interlocutors.role: Phenomenological background; not foregrounded in Kisiel's essay (vs. centrality in Michalski Ch 3).
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: background

section_5_interlocutors.name: Pierre Aubenque (implicit)
section_5_interlocutors.role: French Aristotle-and-rhetoric tradition; not directly cited but resonant with Kisiel's protopolitical reading.
citations: [implicit; cf. Aubenque Le Problème de l'être chez Aristote]
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: background

section_5_interlocutors.name: P. Christopher Smith (implicit)
section_5_interlocutors.role: Hermeneutics of Original Argument; rhetorical-Heideggerian neighborhood; flagged in volume bibliography but not cited in this essay.
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: background

section_5_interlocutors.name: Thucydides
section_5_interlocutors.role: Source of 'unforgettable speeches' that exemplify Greek instinct for 'persuasive power of speech as paradigm of politics.'
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: borrowed (Greek-rhetorical-political tradition as comparator for Führer-rhetoric)

section_5_interlocutors.name: Parmenides
section_5_interlocutors.role: Source of Heidegger's discovery (in SS 1924) that ousia means 'constant presence' for Greek titans (Aristotle included) since Parmenides — 'a major revolution and caesura in his own thought.'
section_5_interlocutors.relationship: philosophical genealogy

section_6_heidegger_loci.context_in_essay: Hearing (akouein) as 'most fundamental mode of perception'; Aristotle's emphasis on hearing in understanding striking; nous as aneu logou (without speech, beyond language).
section_6_heidegger_loci.contributor_use: central — establishes hearing/auditor as ontologically prior to seeing/sayer

section_6_heidegger_loci.context_in_essay: Heidegger's emerging fundamental ontology takes shape and seeks site for rudimentary protopolitics. The basic GA 18 page-range Kisiel returns to throughout for 'rhetorical protopolitics.'
section_6_heidegger_loci.contributor_use: central — primary textual evidence for protopolitical thesis

section_6_heidegger_loci.context_in_essay: Anyone (das Man) as true bearer of universal of averageness = our language (64); domineering prevalence of Anyone in language = doxa, tacit major premises of rhetoric (73).
section_6_heidegger_loci.contributor_use: central — establishes das Man as rhetorical-political category

section_6_heidegger_loci.context_in_essay: Hearing as component first of rhetor sizing up critical speech-situation (104); not-yet-logos appeal of orexis 'is itself a kind of speech' (105); rhetoric 'first not art but power, dynamis' (114).
section_6_heidegger_loci.contributor_use: central — three-fold support for equiprimordiality and dynamis-thesis

section_6_heidegger_loci.context_in_essay: 'Ethos and pathos are constitutive for legein itself' (165); speech finds deepest roots in mood (177).

section_8_tensions.tension: Aristotelian-rhetorical phase (1923-25) vs. Platonic-metontological phase (1933-35): the protopolitics that began as equiprimordial speech-community of doxa becomes a leader-state of guardians-and-three-services. The textual basis shifts from Rhetoric to Republic; the operative ethical category shifts from phronesis-as-listening-to-call-of-conscience to will-of-the-Führer-as-phronetic-grasp-of-kairos.
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: Heidegger applied his 1924 phronesis-framework to the inauthentic-doxa-rhetoric of the Führer state he had earlier diagnosed; the misapplication is internal-to-his-own framework.

section_8_tensions.tension: Metontological-Führer phase (1933-35) vs. Archaic-Poietic-polemos phase (1935-43): Heidegger's growing disenchantment with 'Führer turning from statesmanlike to coercive ways' generates a reduction of polis to a prepolitical originarity of poets/thinkers/statesmen. The displacement is itself an explicit Heideggerian self-critique (GA 39 51).
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: The polemos-phase is Heidegger's exit from his own Führer-state miscalculation, but it abandons rhetoric proper as 'means of communication for sake of agreement' (GA 53 102).

section_8_tensions.tension: Authentic vs. inauthentic doxa within Heidegger's 1924 framework: present in 1924 ('civil rhetoric of Greeks' vs. 'propaganda rhetoric of postwar Weimar') but 'muted in BT.' Resurfaces in Heidegger's 1933 deployment of Aristotelian phronesis to legitimate the Trommelnder-rhetoric he had earlier diagnosed.
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: BT 'mutes' the 1924 authentic/inauthentic-doxa distinction; Heidegger's 1933 Schlageter-speech and Rectoral Address are inauthentic-doxa applications of his own framework.

section_8_tensions.tension: Aristotle's three definitions of human as equiprimordial vs. Aristotle's genus-species treatment of 'man.' Heidegger reads the three Aristotelian definitions (logon echon, zoon politikon, practical being-in-world) as 'equally primordial' but Aristotle himself, in Arendt's gloss (p. 153), tends to 'speak of man in the singular, as if there were such a thing as a single human nature.'

section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: Heidegger's reading of three equiprimordial definitions implicitly criticizes Aristotle's own genus-species approach; Arendt extends this critique.

section_8_tensions.tension: Heidegger's das Man as path OUT (via SZ 298 resolute openness) vs. das Man as Bourdieu/Marcuse/Arendt's TRAP. Kisiel insists both readings are textually grounded: das Man-description IS premonition of totalitarianism (Bourdieu/Marcuse) AND formally outlines escape (Kisiel's SZ 384/298 reading).
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: Kisiel's reading is a partial-acceptance synthesis: das Man IS sociologically diagnostic of Weimar BUT formally outlines the path-out via communication-and-Kampf.

section_8_tensions.tension: Heidegger's silence on his own 1933 commitment vs. the 'bacillus' that infected his thought before the political turn: Arendt 'never addressed Heidegger's brief but fateful commitment to National Socialism' but knew enough to pinpoint the philosophical-mythological source (Folk and Earth, autochthony myth).
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: Arendt's diagnosis (mythologizing-Folk-and-Earth as compensation for early solipsism) is post hoc but textually grounded.

section_8_tensions.tension: Kisiel's rhetorical-protopolitical thesis (Ch 6) vs. Pöggeler's restricted-conception thesis (Ch 7). Kisiel's framework affirms PROTOPOLITICAL reach of GA 18 across Sections I-V, but the table on p. 149 affirms that RHETORIC IS RESTRICTED to Phase 1 (1923-25). Pöggeler reads the restriction as architectural; Kisiel reads it as politically diagnostic.
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: [INTERP-low] Kisiel and Pöggeler converge on the FACT of post-1924 restriction but diverge on its meaning: Kisiel sees the restriction as itself a political-philosophical diagnosis (the Führer-state and polemos-phases are post-rhetorical because Heidegger gave up the protopolitical project); Pöggeler sees the restriction as an architectural limit on rhetoric's reach into Heidegger's thought.

section_8_tensions.tension: Kisiel's exhaustive treatment of Heidegger's Nazi turn (Section VII metontological polis + 1933 Schlageter-speech + Rectoral Address + Führerstaat) vs. Gross's framing (HR-01-GROSS-B Sec. IV) of Heidegger's 'subsequent Nazism' via pathos-genealogy + Luther's Affektenlehre. Both treat the Nazi turn through rhetorical-philosophical lens; Kisiel reads it via phronesis-misapplication, Gross via pathos-as-substrate.
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: [INTERP-low] Kisiel and Gross are mutually reinforcing: Kisiel's phronesis-miscalculation thesis explains WHY Heidegger applied his framework to the Nazi cause (he saw it as kairos-grasping); Gross's pathos-genealogy explains WHAT predisposed Heidegger to mistake propaganda-pathos for civic-pathos.

section_8_tensions.tension: Kisiel's rhetoric-as-dynamis claim (p. 146) vs. the same claim in Gadamer (Ch 2 p. 49). Both essays cite Rhetoric I.2 as authoritative; Gadamer makes the dispute with technē explicit; Kisiel takes the dynamis-reading as granted.
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: Kisiel's protopolitical reading depends on Gadamer's dynamis-reading; the two essays are mutually supportive on this central Aristotelian point.

section_8_tensions.tension: Kisiel's reading of ethos as Heideggerian Entschlossenheit (Section V) vs. Hyde's reading of ethos as call-of-conscience-call-to-character (Ch 4). Both essays translate Aristotelian ethos into BT vocabulary; Kisiel uses Entschlossenheit (SZ §60), Hyde uses Ruf des Gewissens (SZ §§54-60).
section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: Kisiel and Hyde diverge on which BT vocabulary best translates Aristotelian ethos: Kisiel emphasizes deliberative-political ethos (Entschlossenheit + prohairesis); Hyde emphasizes epideictic-existential ethos (Ruf des Gewissens). Both readings are textually grounded; the choice reveals each contributor's rhetorical-genre preference.

section_8_tensions.tension: [INTERP-high] The structural relationship between Kisiel's Section IX (Arendt) and Sections I-VIII (Heidegger): is Arendt the redemption of the protopolitical project Heidegger abandoned, or is she its translation/transformation into post-1945 modernity? The essay reads the Arendtian afterlife as redemptive but stops short of declaring it 'continuous-with' Heidegger's 1923-24 framework.

section_8_tensions.kisiel_diagnosis: [INTERP-high] Kisiel never explicitly resolves whether Arendt is RETRIEVAL (continuous) or TRANSLATION (transformed). The closing critique of Heidegger via Arendt suggests retrieval-with-correction.

section_10_edges.note: Kisiel's protopolitical reading PRESUPPOSES rhetoric is dynamis (capacity for situational insight), not technē (sophist's art of persuasion); the dynamis-reading is what makes rhetoric ontologically equiprimordial with the everyday political speech-situation.
Rhetorical protopolitics IS the rudimentary speech-community whose telos is Verständigung (= hermeneia, coming-to-an-understanding-agreement); GA 18 45f, 122f, 241 ground this identification.

section_10_edges.source: CONCEPT:equiprimordial modes of persuasion and trust
section_10_edges.note: The three pisteis (pathos/ethos/logos) operationalize the equiprimordiality of pistis with aletheia at the level of speech-situation; this is the volume-central reading of GA 18 165 ('ethos and pathos are constitutive for legein itself').

The leveling das Man (= inauthentic doxa of cliché/catchphrase) contrasts with authentic doxa (= 'authentic discoveredness of being-with-one-another'). Both belong to the same rhetorical-ontological register but Heidegger's 1924 framework distinguishes them, while BT 'mutes' the distinction.
SZ 384's pair 'communication and struggle' is the path OUT of the leveling Anyone; Kisiel emphasizes these as 'two rhetorical dimensions' lifting Dasein into authentic historical happening.

Phronesis as receptive response to call of conscience operationalizes the translation of Aristotelian ethos into Heideggerian Entschlossenheit; politician's resoluteness brings others to same resolution = kairos = moment of decision in polity/policy (GA 18 171).

Heidegger's 1933-34 deployment of 'will of leader' is conditioned 'wholly in terms of Aristotle's political virtue, phronesis' — phronesis as 'will deliberatively grasps the situation in the fullness of its time, in it the kairos is at work.' This is Heidegger's phronetic misapplication.

The metontological polis = the Führerstaat: two basic existentials (people + state), Führer principle, guardians (Hüter), three-level service (labor/defense/knowledge), highest actualization of human being in the state. Plato's Republic as basic text.

Heidegger's growing disenchantment with Führer-state historicizes the metontological polis into the archaic-poietic polemos-polis; the 1935+ poets/thinkers/statesmen polis is the historical successor to the 1933-35 Führer-state.

Polemos as combative-conversation operationalizes the archaic-poietic polis: 'Conversation here is not communication, but the fundamental happening of radical exposure in the thick of beings' (GA 53 102).

Sophocles' Antigone glossed as hypsipolis apolis (lofty-city/no-city) exemplifies the archaic-poietic polis-vocation: lofty greatness creating new home for people, also precipitous destruction. Schlageter, Hölderlin, Nietzsche, van Gogh share this fate.

section_10_edges.note: Arendt's radicalized Mitwelt operationalizes as the public space of doxa (dokein in twofold sense: opinion AND splendor/fame). The 'space of appearance' is where 'I go public, make my debut.'

section_10_edges.target: CONCEPT:equiprimordial modes of persuasion and trust
section_10_edges.note: Arendt's twofold doxa (Ansicht / Ansehen) refines the Aristotelian rhetorical speech-situation: doxic content of speech itself + ethos of speaker before judgment of audience.

Kant's 'enlarged mentality' (Critique of Judgment §40) refines Aristotelian phronesis as the cosmopolitan-judgmental ability to 'take account of mode of representation of all other men'; converges with Aristotle's phronesis kai arete kai eunoia (Rhetoric 2.1, 1378a10).

Heidegger's Folk-and-Earth autochthony-myth supplies the metontological polis with mythological ground; Arendt diagnoses this as 'mechanical reconciliation of atomized selves in a common ground alien to their nature.'

The 1923 annus terribilis historicizes the figure of modern Dasein as newspaper-reader: postwar pulp media transmitting party-political speech 'from far and wide.' Context-dependent textuality replaces oral polis.

Heidegger's May 26, 1933 Schlageter speech (GA 16 759f) exemplifies the rhetorical entry into the metontological polis: epideictic celebration of 'hardest death' of native son operating politically to mobilize Volksgemeinschaft.
Heidegger's GA 18 114 ('rhetoric is first not art but power, dynamis') operationalizes Aristotle's Rhetoric I.2 (rhetoric as dynamis); this is the central rhetorical-ontological bridge of Section V.

Heidegger's GA 18 165 ('ethos and pathos are constitutive for legein itself') refines Aristotle's Rhetoric II three-pisteis-doctrine by reading the three modes as equiprimordial-disclosive-of-being-in (Befindlichkeit/Verstehen/Rede).

SZ 298 ('authentic with-one-another arises from authentic self-being of resolute openness') supports SZ 384's path of 'communication and struggle' out of the leveling Anyone; together they constitute the BT framework of Mitsein-as-historical-happening.

SZ 122 (with SZ 298) operationalizes the leaping-ahead-liberating vs. leaping-in-dominating distinction in Fürsorge; politician projects self as authentic conscience for other in former mode, makes other dependent in latter (welfare-state-mode).

GA 39 51 ('These [Nazi] enthusiasts are now suddenly discovering the political everywhere... But the polis cannot be defined politically') undermines the metontological polis from within Heidegger's WS 1934-35 lectures; this is Heidegger's own self-critique of his earlier Nazi commitment.
GA 53 102 IS the definitional locus for polemos-as-conversation: 'Conversation here is not communication, but the fundamental happening of radical exposure in the thick of beings.'

Arendt's Human Condition refines Heidegger's Mitwelt as space of plurality-and-natality; Arendt's Aristotelian-Kantian convergence (phronesis-arete-eunoia / sensus communis) recovers the protopolitical strand Heidegger abandoned in 1933.

Arendt's diagnosis of Heidegger's Folk-and-Earth mythologizing (autochthony-myth of landed gentry) undermines Heidegger's metontological-polis ground; the autochthony-myth is 'mechanical reconciliation of atomized selves in common ground alien to their nature.'

CROSS-ESSAY EDGE — Kisiel's three-phase model (Phenomenological/Metontological/Archaic-Poietic) contrasts with Pöggeler's monolithic 'restricted conception' thesis: both contributors agree rhetoric is restricted to Phase 1 (1923-25), but Kisiel reads the restriction as politically diagnostic (Heidegger's phronetic-miscalculation generates the post-rhetorical phases), while Pöggeler reads the restriction as architectural (rhetoric is a circumscribed moment that gives way to topology of being).

CROSS-ESSAY EDGE — Kisiel's phronesis-miscalculation thesis (Heidegger applied his 1924 framework to inauthentic-doxa Nazi-rhetoric) refines Gross's pathos-as-substrate genealogy (HR-01-GROSS-B Sec. IV) by explaining HOW Heidegger came to mistake propaganda-pathos for civic-pathos: through Aristotelian phronesis applied to kairos that he misread.

CROSS-ESSAY EDGE — Kisiel's protopolitical thesis presupposes Gadamer's dynamis-reading (Ch 2 p. 49: 'Aristotle defined rhetoric (1.2) as dynamis. This definition is to be retained even though Aristotle often designates it as technē'). Kisiel cites GA 18 114 to operationalize the same Aristotelian point.

CROSS-ESSAY EDGE — Kisiel's ethos = Entschlossenheit (deliberative-political register, SZ §60) contrasts with Hyde's ethos = Ruf des Gewissens (epideictic-existential register, SZ §§54-60). Both translate Aristotelian ethos into BT vocabulary; the choice of rhetorical genre (deliberative vs. epideictic) marks the divergence.

CROSS-ESSAY EDGE — Kisiel's protopolitical reading supports Struever's rhetoric-as-life-science thesis: both treat rhetoric as politically and temporally indispensable, both anchor in GA 18 SS 1924, both share the dynamis-not-techne reading.

CROSS-ESSAY EDGE — Kisiel's archaic-poietic phase (1935-43, Sophocles Antigone, polemos) is the same textual territory as Pöggeler's 'topology of being'; Kisiel reads it as Heidegger's exit from Führer-state misapplication, Pöggeler reads it as Heidegger's positive resolution. Same texts (GA 39, GA 53), opposed valence.
